title: Ravel’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage. For composers outside the symphonic tradition it asks for an honest counterfactual.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Ravel’s Missing Symphony (work id ravel-symphony-1)

Honest counterfactual: Ravel wrote no symphony and distrusted the form. His multi-movement abstract works are chamber music and the two piano concertos; his orchestral works are ballets, dances and orchestrations. This piece imagines a compact “Symphonie en ré” that borrows the four-movement plan of his String Quartet and Sonatine (moderate first movement, quick pizzicato scherzo with a slow middle, very slow movement, fast finale in an uneven metre) and scores it for his kind of orchestra. No theme is taken from Ravel.

Orchestra (14 staves, sounding pitch): 2 flutes, 2 oboes, cor anglais, 2 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 4 horns, 2 trumpets, harp, celesta, strings. No timpani or percussion.

Language: modes instead of major and minor (Dorian on D, Aeolian on A), chords of the seventh and ninth and with added sixths as the normal consonances, melodies doubled at the octave by unlike instruments, harp and celesta figuration, parallel chord motion. Because of this the usual checks are relaxed for this work: half-step clashes inside chords and parallel fifths and octaves are part of the style and are not reported.

Movements
I. Modéré, 3/4, D Dorian: sonata form in miniature; second theme in F for cor anglais, returning in D major.
II. Assez vif, 6/8, A minor: scherzo with the strings plucked throughout the fast sections, and a slow bowed middle for cor anglais.
III. Très lent, 3/4, B flat: a long flute melody over a slow waltz-like accompaniment of harp and strings.
IV. Vif, 5/8, D: a short finale in a three-plus-two metre.

Target length about ten minutes; the conciseness is deliberate. Compromise known from the start: melodies and the chord of every bar are written by hand; a program writes harp and celesta figuration, held chords and the fuller textures from the chord plan.

Published live draft revision 1 with this public change note:
First playable draft: the whole first movement — a calm Dorian theme for clarinet and flute, a second theme in F for cor anglais over harp, a short development that climbs by minor thirds, and a reprise that ends in D major.

entries.text:
Published live draft revision 2 with this public change note:
Complete, revised draft: added the plucked scherzo with its slow bowed middle, the very slow movement for flute over harp, and the finale in five-eight; in revision the idle woodwind were given parts in the slow movement and the celesta added to the finale. This revision matches the published score.

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text: Build m2: write the score, check bar lengths, ranges, sustained notes and half-step clashes, validate with the site validator, compare with abcjs playback, and count parallel fifths/octaves between the outer voices. Second movement rebuilt: the change from plucked to bowed strings for the slow middle section (and back) was being ignored by the site's notation library because the instruction stood at the start of a line; it is now written at the end of the preceding line. Checked in the library's audio sequence: the first-violin notes now carry program 45 (pizzicato), 48 (bowed) and 45 again.
